subject: anatomy
title: Connective tissue, cartilage and bone histology: high-yield essentials

steps.tx: Connective tissue is made of cells, **ground substance** and fibres. The main cell is the fibroblast, which secretes collagen and elastin. Mast cells are a prominent source of histamine. Collagen is the most abundant protein in the body, and its fibres show a triple-stranded, quarter-staggered arrangement of tropocollagen molecules, which aids mineralisation of bone.

steps.tx: Perichondrium is a connective tissue sheath around cartilage. Chondrocytes are nourished by **diffusion** through the matrix from vessels outside the cartilage, because cartilage is avascular. Hyaline cartilage lacks blood vessels, lymphatics and nerves. Growth of cartilage is appositional when perichondrium is present and interstitial when it is absent.

vis.alt: Three cartilage types shown as microscopic motifs: hyaline with paired chondrocytes in clear matrix, elastic with a dense network of elastic fibres, fibrocartilage with parallel collagen bundles and rows of cells, with sites and perichondrium status listed.
vis.caption: Hyaline and elastic cartilage have a perichondrium; fibrocartilage and articular cartilage do not, so they heal poorly.

steps.tx: Bone is made of **osteoblasts**, which are protein-secreting cells with abundant rough endoplasmic reticulum and Golgi, and make type I collagen. **Osteoclasts** are multinucleated cells of monocyte-macrophage origin that resorb bone, sitting in Howship's lacunae. **Osteocytes** are osteoblasts trapped in their own matrix, lying in lacunae and linked by canaliculi.

Osteoclasts are multinucleated cells of monocyte-macrophage origin that resorb bone, sitting in Howship's lacunae. Osteocytes are osteoblasts trapped in their own matrix, lying in lacunae and linked by canaliculi.

steps.tx: Mature bone is **lamellar** bone. In compact bone, lamellae form concentric cylinders called the Haversian system or osteon, centred on a Haversian canal. Volkmann canals run transversely to connect Haversian canals. Spongy or cancellous bone, found at epiphyses and in vertebrae, has no Haversian systems; its canaliculi open into marrow cavities. Woven bone is seen in fetal bone and fracture healing.

steps.tx: In **endochondral ossification**, a cartilage model is replaced by bone. The growth plate has zones: resting, proliferative, hypertrophic, calcified and ossification. Chondrocytes stack in columns in the proliferative zone and enlarge in the hypertrophic zone, where the matrix calcifies. Periosteum supplies osteoblasts that make the major share of new bone after a fracture. Remember that most long bones are preformed in hyaline cartilage, except the clavicle.
